project.name: l3i
project.summary: The Luau runtime for DreamWeave: a Rust binder that owns its Luau 0.740 build, plans every VM before it exists, and lowers hot script calls to native code.

notes.summary: Textual identity as dense numbers with `@dream/intern`, lowered so a repeated identity never leaves native code; a zstd encoder; a constant that says whether a build used the verified toolchain; a slow path for lowering hooks that stays native; and cheaper string, buffer and optional arguments for every binding.
added: `@dream/intern` (feature `intern`): pools that turn strings or buffer spans into dense number tokens under `exact` or `ascii-nocase` equality, folding case inside the hash and the comparison, so no lowered copy is made and a repeated identity allocates nothing. `find`, `resolve` to the first spelling seen, and `interner()` for interpreted code.

Under `jit`, an annotated `dream_intern_Pool`'s `intern` and `find` lower to native code: a case-insensitive duplicate costs 315 instructions against 1378 for `string.lower` and a table lookup, and an insert or a bad argument runs the bound method without leaving native code.
`IrBuilder::namecall_call`: the namecall and call Luau would have emitted, as a userdata namecall hook's slow path.
`l3i::VERIFIED_TOOLCHAIN`: `true` exactly when `build.rs` found the verified toolchain, whether or not `L3I_UNVERIFIED_TOOLCHAIN` was set, for hosts that publish performance numbers.
`@dream/bytes`'s `zstdCompress`, through ruzstd's one implemented level; any other level is refused by name.
`Runtime::registered_require_modules`: every path registered with `register_require_module`, the plan's included, in registration order.
changed: `Q:fromXYZW` lowers to native code: 93 instructions against the binder's 459.

String, buffer and string-or-buffer arguments are read straight from Luau's value layout (54 instructions instead of 293), and a trailing optional argument is read once (two optional integers cost 335 fewer instructions).
fixed: A lowered rotation packs with the omitted component's own sign, so a quarter turn whose two largest components tie with opposite signs no longer packs a different rotation.

notes.summary: Chunks load on any scope's thread under the runtime's native code policy, the code generator is reachable from a call, templates resolve their imports at load time, and a frame's call site costs two debug fields.
added: `source::LoadScope`, implemented for every scope: `load_bytecode` and `load_source` load a chunk on the scope's own thread, so Luau resolves its builtin imports against that thread's safe globals, and compile it natively according to the runtime's mode, so a `require` written in Rust needs neither the `Runtime` nor `luau_load` by hand.
`NativeCodeGen::for_scope`: the runtime's code generator from a bound function's `Call` or any other scope of its VM.
`DebugScope::call_site`: the chunk name and current line of a frame, asking Luau for those two fields only; Luau records lines, not columns.

Templates load on a loader thread whose globals are the base environment, so Luau resolves their builtin imports when the template loads and every instance takes the fast import path from its first run.

notes.summary: First release: the whole Luau 0.740 C API under a scoped Rust layer, planned runtimes composed from extensions, sandboxes, the dream-net bridge in every VM, and native lowering hooks written in Rust.
added: The typed binder: `Runtime::bind_function` reads arguments straight from Luau's 16-byte value layout, with OpenMW's optional, variadic and overload rules and its exact error wording.

Tagged and untagged userdata per runtime: the same Rust type may be tag 8 in one VM, 17 in another, and untagged in a third; generated `__index` and `__namecall` dispatchers that cost one Luau call frame.

Runtime plans: an `Extension` describes modules, userdata, packed kinds, services and capabilities without a VM, and `RuntimePlan::finalize` assigns tags, compiler slots, atoms and direct slots, validates every identifier and path, and renders the `.d.luau` for the composition.
Sandboxes with OpenMW's prelude, per-script instances, and compiled templates cloned per script.
The `dream.net` bridge in every plan: schemas, clients gated by the `network.transport` capability, host-created servers, and `pollInto` with one payload copy and no allocation.
Packed 64-bit scalars with a kind registry: `dream.quat` rotations and animation keys, `dream.raster` colours and clip rectangles, and `dream.soft_render` behind the `soft-render` feature.
Native code generation (`jit`): Luau's CodeGen with lowering hooks written in Rust against an `IrBuilder` C ABI; quaternion, colour and vertex-writer paths that lower to IR with no C call.
Luau's Analysis frontend (`analysis`): type checker, linter and autocomplete over a source provider, definition files, and the gate that type checks a plan's declared API against strict scripts.

`@dream/bytes` (`bytes`) for parsing foreign file formats in script: searching, record strings, varints, big-endian, 24-bit and half-float reads with a receiver lowered to native code, and behind their own features the codecs (DEFLATE, LZ4, zstd, LZMA), the digests (CRC-32 to BLAKE3) and the text codepages, all pure Rust.

Watchdog limits, memory categories, call scopes, collector control and the profiler plumbing OpenMW's engine needs, and every function in `lua.h`, `lualib.h`, `luacode.h`, `luacodegen.h`, `luajitinliner.h` and `Require.h` declared by hand.
The clang, lld and cross-language thin LTO toolchain, enforced by `build.rs` and measured in TOOLCHAIN.md: a bound call within forty instructions of a bare C function.
Templates load from any thread of the VM: `Sandbox::load_template_in` takes only the scope, so a `require` loader captures the sandbox and nothing else.
Rust 1.92, clang and lld; dream-net 1.1.0.
